messages:
Sasha: Heads up — AcmeIngest (dedicated/private) reporting intermittent 401s for API key auth when requests go through their internal LB -> our VPC L7 proxy. Direct hits to the service (bypassing LB) succeed. Repro steps below.

Sasha: Repro (from their env):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED' https://api.acme.internal/v1/ingest
* Connected to lb.internal (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/ingest HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.acme.internal
> Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "missing or invalid api_key"
}
```

Sasha: But when they curl the node directly (10.0.8.9) visiting the same service port, same auth header -> 200. Customer says header seems to be mutated/dropped by the LB path.

Anu: Thanks — can we get full request headers from the LB side and a dump from our L7 proxy? Also what LB type is this (nginx/nginx-ingress/TCP LB/ALB)?

Sasha: It's an internal haproxy-based LB (they manage it), then GCP NLB -> our VPC ingress (Envoy). They forwarded a pcap and an Envoy access log snippet. I'll paste minimal relevant parts.

Sasha: LB-side tcpdump shows the Authorization header present on outbound to NLB. Envoy access log for the request hitting our edge:
```
[2026-01-12T15:03:21.123Z] "GET /v1/ingest" 401 - upstream_transport_failure - - "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" "x-forwarded-for: 10.2.3.4" "x-envoy-original-path: /v1/ingest"
```

Kyle: Interesting — Envoy log includes Authorization in the string above but our auth layer returns 401 with message about missing api_key. That suggests our authz service (ext_authz) may be receiving a different header set or Authorization being rewritten before authz check. Marcos, any ext_authz quirks you recall?

Marcos: Yep — in some older ext_authz configs we intentionally scrub certain headers before calling the auth service, to avoid leaking internal tokens. We have a list of allowed_headers that are forwarded to the auth service. If Authorization isn't in that allowlist, the auth server never sees it and returns missing API key.

Marcos: Can you paste our ext_authz config for that cluster? I want to check allowed_headers / headers_to_add / clear_route.

Sasha: Pasted the snapshot from the customer's cluster (they're using our private package with Istio + envoy ext_authz):
```
apiVersion: "security.istio.io/v1beta1"
kind: "RequestAuthentication"
# ...
ext_authz:
  allowed_headers: ["x-request-id","x-forwarded-for","x-customer-id"]
  allowed_client_headers: []
  headers_to_add: []
  disable_send_headers: true
```

Anu: There it is — allowed_headers doesn't include Authorization and disable_send_headers: true will drop unspecified headers. That would explain why auth service never saw the Authorization header during ext_authz check.

Kyle: Is this config global? We pushed a more restrictive template to Dedicated clusters a while back for compliance, and a few customers have custom LBs which re-order header casing and sometimes change header names (e.g., lowercasing). If we don't explicitly include 'authorization' (lowercase) it might be excluded. Envoy header matching is case-insensitive but our config list strings might be normalized.

Marcos: Quick workaround: update allowed_headers to include both 'authorization' and 'Authorization' or better, normalize to lowercase in the config processor. For a targeted fix we can add 'authorization' to allowed_headers for that tenant's policy.

Sasha: Customer asked for a reproducible patch they can apply without a full redeploy. They can inject a header preserve rule at their HAProxy to move the token into X-Forwarded-Authorization as a stopgap. Example: `http-request add-header X-Forwarded-Authorization "%[req.hdr(Authorization)]"`.

Anu: That helps short-term but we should fix server-side. Marcos, can we push a hotfix template to dedicated tenants that adds 'authorization' to allowed_headers and flips disable_send_headers=false? Any security concerns?

Marcos: If we set disable_send_headers=false, more headers will flow to ext_authz, which might include sensitive internal headers. Better to explicitly add 'authorization' only. That should be safe. We'll also add a validation that we don't accidentally add weird cookies.

Kyle: Also check our header canonicalization in the envoy filter processor — some setups convert to lowercase keys. I'll add a small code change to match header names case-insensitively when evaluating allowed_headers.

Sasha: For the customer: we asked them to try two things concurrently: 1) temporary HAProxy rule to mirror Authorization into X-Forwarded-Authorization and 2) we applied a tenant-scoped policy adding 'authorization' to allowed_headers. Will update here with results.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: patch/tenant-policy-add-authz-header -> dedicated-cluster-acme (canary 1/2)

Sasha: Patch is live on canary node, customer testing now.

Sasha: Customer confirms after canary patch -> their requests now return 200 consistently. They also removed the HAProxy workaround and it's still working. :tada:

Anu: Follow-up actions:
- Marcos/Kyle to ship a small change to the template to include 'authorization' in allowed_headers for Dedicated tenants that opt into external auth.
- Marcos to add a config lint rule that warns when disable_send_headers=true and 'authorization' not present.
- Support to notify impacted customers and provide HAProxy workaround snippet.

Marcos: I'll open PRs for the template change and the lint rule.

Kyle: I'll add an e2e test in the ingress suite that simulates an external LB that mutates headers to ensure we keep Authorization forwarded to ext_authz.

Sasha: Closing loop with the customer and marking this incident as resolved once PRs merged. Good catch everyone.
